column11: | RT-1 | **A `hwbp.py` run left the game wedged after detach — 0.02 s of CPU across 3 s wall, 99 threads alive.** The run itself succeeded (control 171 hits, target 9+9), and the wedge was only noticed because three key presses aimed at the front-end did nothing and a screenshot showed the game still on the Square Enix splash a minute later. `hwbp.py` clears the debug registers in a `finally` and calls `DebugActiveProcessStop` with an unchecked pre-attach `DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(FALSE)` (protection was not verified; [EXP-017](../_experiments/EXP-017-debugger-exit-policy.md) later corrects and tests that setup) — but it clears them across `threads_of(pid)` **enumerated at detach time**, so a thread created during the run could keep a programmed DR7 and take debug traps with no debugger attached. **That is a hypothesis, not a finding**; the correlation is one run. This matters beyond one experiment: **a runtime instrument that leaves the target unusable makes every later observation in the same session worthless**, and nothing currently checks the target is still running afterwards. Related: an earlier session recorded a *different* wedge — during the run, fixed by restricting context writes to the trapping thread. **CORRECTED 2026-09-08, the same day it was filed: the hypothesis is wrong.** Three controlled runs — attach-only (`--no-arm`, 21.4 % of a core), armed on a settled game (39.1 %), and armed during the boot sequence with 123 threads (34.4 %) — all left the game **alive**, against a no-attach baseline of 23.4 %. `hwbp.py` is exonerated for this configuration and the stale-DR7 mechanism is unsupported. **The wedge itself was real** (0.02 s across 3 s wall) and its cause is **unknown**; the block that observed it also ran `window_focus.py` and `runtime_input_probe.py` three times in between, and **none of those was tested**. Liveness is now measured by `process_liveness.py` as a rate rather than judged. **UPDATED 2026-09-08 — it is STATE-DEPENDENT, and the withdrawal above was drawn from the wrong state.** Three pre-load runs are clean; **two in-world runs both wedged the game and it never recovered** — one open-ended with a per-frame control (hwbp's own liveness check reported `FROZEN`, 0 hits on everything), one tightly bounded at 60 hits in 0.2 s wall (still 1.6 % and falling afterwards). **So hit rate is not the mechanism**, and neither is thread count (101 in-world vs 105 and 123 pre-load). The practical constraint on goal 3: **a capture from a loaded save costs the session that save**, which the ~2-minute reload recipe in §4bk makes affordable but which must be planned for. | OPEN |
